newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-FIFA CONTEMPLATES PENSIONS FOR REFEREES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA CONTEMPLATES PENSIONS FOR REFEREES.

text.p: International soccer chiefs are contemplating setting up a fund to guarantee referees a pension in a bid to stamp out corruption in the sport.
The world governing body FIFA believes referees are at their most vulnerable to bribes in the last few years of their career when they are thinking about their financial future.
The idea of a fund, which would take referees one step closer to being professional, was discussed at a meeting of FIFA's fair play committee on Thursday.
"We want to get rid of the temptation to do something incorrect. We realise that the two or three years before a referee retires is a crucial period, " FIFA spokesman Keith Cooper said.

"The referee has a lot of power then. He is surrounded by young millionaires who get a lot from the game and he gets nothing in his pocket. We want to stop the temptation that the referee might have to cash in."
International soccer was recently hit by a bribery scandal involving a former leading referee. Some top figures in the game believe referees should become professionals.
The proposals for the fund were discussed in detail and will be put to a meeting of FIFA's executive committee here at the weekend.
The ever-increasing influence of big business and television is also to be discussed by the executive board.

FIFA is concerned that some companies are influencing the fixture lists too much by setting up international friendlies between teams which they sponsor. This can put players in a difficult position regarding their commitment to club and country.

The trend in many European countries for football to be played virtually every day of the week because of television is also worrying the governing body. It believes there is a danger the public might be bombarded with too much soccer and get bored.
The fair play committee also discussed proposals for a world seminar on racism in the game which may take place later this year.
